scope.selection: P00-listed current app/config/migrations plus backup/restore and ledger runbooks; installed framework crypto evidence explicitly separate
limits: lexical matches are review anchors, not proof of runtime activation or complete dataflow
schema matches include historical migrations/down paths, not a claim every object exists now
asset field declarations can outlive current filesystem content
unknown source columns or production object differences require H0/P03 explicit mapping; no generic production sanitizer

classification_policy.encrypted_cast: decrypt/authenticate in private boundary; map sensitive content; reencrypt isolated derived key before insert
classification_policy.crypt_call: opaque tokens/cursors/session/update payloads; not necessarily persistent database columns
classification_policy.keyed_digest: preserve caller-specific key and normalization; classify output encoding at callsite
classification_policy.digest_or_constant_time_comparison: not automatically secret or HMAC; money/source fingerprints protected unchanged
classification_policy.password_or_auth: P02 fixture uses unusable markers without auth compatibility claims; P03 fixtures claiming parity must preserve scheme/KDF and use isolated credentials
classification_policy.file_or_asset_reference: classify bytes and reference separately; synthetic per-bot remap where needed
classification_policy.schema_object: capture actual catalog definition/state at H0; preserve constraints/triggers; roles/grants separate from dump
classification_policy.key_configuration: names only; secret values transferred separately
classification_policy.acquisition_entrypoint: documentation evidence only; default production scripts not invoked for migration

key_contracts.usage: AES-256-CBC; base64: keys decoded by EncryptionServiceProvider; previous keys decrypt only; no actual keys acquired
key_contracts.derived_policy: new isolated key; decrypt authenticated source then transform and re-encrypt before INSERT

key_contracts.usage: literal config string bytes, not decoded cipher key; HMAC-SHA256 lowercase hex unless caller explicitly requests binary/truncation
key_contracts.derived_policy: new isolated key; recompute only mapped non-financial bindings; preserve protected economic fingerprints

key_contracts.usage: trimmed override or persisted storage/app/private/credential-identity-fingerprint.key; HMAC-SHA256 normalized identity; key digest SHA256; generated secret is hex of 32 random bytes
key_contracts.derived_policy: separate isolated stable secret; mapped values and registry fingerprints/readiness digest must agree

key_contracts.usage: trimmed configured waitlist key or literal APP_KEY fallback; HMAC-SHA256 lower/trim normalized email
key_contracts.derived_policy: recompute alongside encrypted mapped email; preserve equality/cardinality

key_contracts.usage: provider-specific signatures, not credential identity or cipher keys
key_contracts.derived_policy: synthetic inert targets and secrets; never use real provider credentials in derived runtime

key_contracts.usage: backup transport encryption distinct from Laravel fields, HMAC, fingerprint and database credentials
key_contracts.derived_policy: separate archive decryption custody; never include in provenance or source bundle

file_classes.policy: owner-reviewed synthetic replacement or approved non-sensitive copy; preserve dimensions/type/reference edges; public location is not confidentiality proof
replace with synthetic non-payable template; do not copy real QR payment targets

roots: private source only; remote Telegram media may have no local bytes
file_classes.policy: no real customer proof/receipt/credential artifact in derived output; synthetic placeholder retaining relationship, class and availability state

roots: Telegram remote reference; navigation/draft payloads also reference media
file_classes.policy: map by source bot plus source file reference to testing bot plus synthetic target; file_unique_id is correlation not reusable download/send authorization; unknown bytes remain unavailable
secret-channel transfer only; excluded from ordinary asset archive and derived public files
do not restore runnable queues/sessions/log bodies into derived app; classify protected content before removal from acquisition; do not delete durable database obligations/history

schema_capture_required: schemas and relation/column types, nullability, defaults, generated/identity definitions, collations
PK/FK including validation/deferrability/action, CHECK/UNIQUE/exclusion constraints and indexes including predicates
functions/procedures/triggers with definitions, enabled state, owners and security-definer/search_path facts
views/materialized views, rules, RLS policies and enable/force state
roles without password hashes, role attributes/membership, owners, database/schema/table/function/sequence ACL and default privileges
extensions/version/schema, shared_preload_libraries prerequisites such as pg_stat_statements
sequences ownership/dependency, start/increment/min/max/cache/cycle, last_value/is_called; migration history
tablespaces/publications/subscriptions/foreign servers if present: capture metadata privately; do not recreate outbound connectivity

matches.source: `scripts/balance-restore-drill.sh` executes this whole procedure against a disposable PostgreSQL 16 container: it migrates a fresh database, seeds one Customer with a settled USDT credit, one pending balance delivery effect and one unsettled funding target, takes a `pg_dump`, destroys and restores the database, then runs `restore-open → restore-replay → reconcile → restore-close` and finally re-checks that the ledger/receipt/claim row counts and balances are exactly what the dump contained. It never touches production data:
CREATE ROLE lhie_app_runtime LOGIN PASSWORD '<from secret manager>';
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO lhie_app_runtime;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON customer_usdt_balance_accounts TO lhie_app_runtime;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON customer_usdt_balance_entries TO lhie_app_runtime;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON customer_usdt_balance_accounting_events TO lhie_app_runtime;
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO lhie_app_runtime;
-- Explicitly remove mutation rights in case an earlier grant included them.
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON customer_usdt_balance_entries FROM lhie_app_runtime;
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON customer_usdt_balance_accounting_events FROM lhie_app_runtime;
for dotenv_key in GPG_RECIPIENT GPG_PASSPHRASE POSTGRES_PASSWORD POSTGRES_DB POSTGRES_USER DB_SERVICE; do
printf 'Backup encryption is required: set GPG_RECIPIENT or GPG_PASSPHRASE.\n' >&2
printf 'Set only one backup encryption mode: GPG_RECIPIENT or GPG_PASSPHRASE.\n' >&2
printf 'Refusing destructive restore. Set RESTORE_CONFIRM=yes or pass --yes.\n' >&2
printf 'GPG_PASSPHRASE is required for encrypted backups.\n' >&2

gpg --batch --decrypt --passphrase "$GPG_PASSPHRASE" "$BACKUP_FILE" | gzip -dc | $COMPOSE exec -T -e PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-}" "$DB_SERVICE" psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
